questions.question: Footrests:

options.text: Can be shared by the driver and passenger
Are required for the driver and passenger

questions.correctAnswerText: Are required for the driver and passenger
questions.explanation: Keep your feet on the footrests for balance. Motorcycles must have footrests for passengers. Firm footing keeps your passenger from falling off and pulling you off the bike too.

questions.question: Long-term exposure to wind noise:

options.text: Is a normal part of riding a motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Wind noise can permanently damage your hearing over time. Wear ear protection when riding. This protects your hearing while still letting you hear important sounds like sirens and car horns.

questions.question: When riding, your feet should be:
questions.explanation: Keep your feet on the footrests while riding to maintain proper balance.

questions.question: If you are in a collision, you must report it to law enforcement if it results in:
questions.explanation: In Wyoming, you must report a collision to authorities if it causes an injury, death, or property damage of $1,000 or more.

questions.question: When stopping your motorcycle with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Ride faster than you normally would.
Start slowing down earlier than you normally would.
Merge into smaller traffic gaps than you normally would.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down earlier than you normally would.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. The extra weight makes the motorcycle slower to speed up, slow down, and turn. When carrying a passenger, reduce your speed, slow down earlier when stopping, and look for larger gaps when turning or merging into traffic.

questions.question: You must have ______ insurance to legally operate a motor vehicle.
questions.explanation: Your license can be suspended if you operate a motor vehicle without liability insurance.

questions.question: As you approach a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Move to the part of the lane where other drivers can see you most easily.
Move to the part of the lane closest to the traffic control device.
Move to the outside edge of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the part of the lane where other drivers can see you most easily.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, move to the part of your lane that puts you in another driver's view as soon as possible.

questions.question: The best clothing for a motorcyclist:

options.text: Should not stand out to other drivers.

questions.explanation: Good riding clothing protects you in a crash, keeps you comfortable, and makes you visible to other drivers.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They warn drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that a divided roadway is ahead.

questions.question: The best footwear for motorcyclists:
questions.explanation: Leather boots give the best foot protection when riding. Choose boots that are high enough to cover and support your ankles.

questions.question: Locking your brakes can:
questions.explanation: Locking the brakes can cause you to lose control. If your front brake locks, release it and then apply it again. If your rear brake locks when stopping on a surface with good grip, keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: Pick a lane position that:

options.text: Makes you more visible and gives you safe space around your bike.
You like, without thinking about other riders.
Gets you close to other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes you more visible and gives you safe space around your bike.
questions.explanation: Position yourself where other road users can see you best. Keep space around your motorcycle at all times. Change your position as road conditions change. There is no single best lane position for all situations.

questions.question: A protective jacket should:

options.text: Be loose and flap in the wind while riding.

questions.explanation: Riding clothes should protect you and keep you comfortable. Jackets and pants should fit snug enough that they do not flap in the wind, but loose enough that you can move freely.

questions.question: Before every ride, you should:

options.text: Check that your bike's brake lights work.
Check that the paint is not peeling.
Make sure your bike is completely clean.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that your bike's brake lights work.
questions.explanation: Do safety checks before every ride. Test each brake to make sure the brake lights turn on.

questions.question: A flat front tire is especially dangerous because:

options.text: The front tire controls steering, which controls your balance.
A flat front tire will disable the front brake.
A flat front tire will stop you from speeding up.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front tire controls steering, which controls your balance.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire is dangerous because it affects your steering, which affects your balance. If steering feels heavy, you might have a flat front tire.

questions.question: Pick a lane position that:

options.text: Helps you stay away from road hazards.
Hides you from other road users.
Places you right next to another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps you stay away from road hazards.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you avoid road hazards. Always keep safe space around your motorcycle.

questions.question: Experienced riders use a system called SIPDE. What does the "I" stand for?
questions.explanation: Experienced riders use SIPDE to make safe decisions while riding. SIPDE stands for Scan, Identify, Predict, Decide, and Execute.

questions.question: Which color makes you less visible to other drivers?
questions.explanation: Wear bright orange, red, yellow, or green to be more visible. Avoid dark or drab colors while riding.

questions.question: After riding over something on the road, you should:

options.text: Keep riding because the danger is gone.
Pull over and check your tires and rims for damage.
Stop to remove the object from the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check your tires and rims for damage.
questions.explanation: After riding over an object, pull off the road and check your tires and rims for damage. Also check that nothing is caught in the chain or belt before continuing.

questions.question: When stopping, you should:
questions.explanation: Get used to using both the front and rear brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What color are service signs?
questions.explanation: Service signs are blue with white letters. They show where to find rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: Two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time. What should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
You should flash your headlight to signal the other vehicle to proceed.
You should continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: What is the only way to remove alcohol from your system?
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to remove alcohol. Nothing can speed up this process.

questions.question: You see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop on the road behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait until the emergency vehicle moves.
Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes to give it extra space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: How should a protective jacket fit?

options.text: Loosely so it flaps in the wind.
Snugly so it does not flap in the wind.
Made of thin material that is easy to move in.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snugly so it does not flap in the wind.
questions.explanation: Your jacket should fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind. It should be made of leather or sturdy material, but still loose enough to move freely.
